=== Task.v ===
Require Import SysF SemiU Reduction.

Theorem reduction : LU2SemiU ⪯ SysF_TYP.

=== Task.v.orig ===
Require Import SysF SemiU Reduction.

Theorem reduction : LU2SemiU ⪯ SysF_TYP.

=== SemiU.v ===
(* Author: Andrej Dudenhefner. From SemiUnification/SemiU.v. *)

Inductive term : Set :=
  | atom : nat -> term
  | arr : term -> term -> term.

Definition valuation : Set := nat -> term.

(* substitute atoms n of a term t by (f n) *)
Fixpoint substitute (f: valuation) (t: term) : term :=
  match t with
  | atom n => f n
  | arr s t => arr (substitute f s) (substitute f t)
  end.

(* The two inequalities share the same left-hand side s. *)
Definition LU2SemiU : term * term * term -> Prop :=
  fun '(s, t0, t1) => exists (φ ψ0 ψ1: valuation),
    substitute ψ0 (substitute φ s) = substitute φ t0 /\ substitute ψ1 (substitute φ s) = substitute φ t1.

=== SysF.v ===
From Stdlib Require Import List.

(* pure lambda-terms M, N, .. *)
Inductive pure_term : Type :=
  | pure_var : nat -> pure_term
  | pure_app : pure_term -> pure_term -> pure_term
  | pure_abs : pure_term -> pure_term.

(* polymorphic types s, t, ..*)
Inductive poly_type : Type :=
  | poly_var : nat -> poly_type
  | poly_arr : poly_type -> poly_type -> poly_type
  | poly_abs : poly_type -> poly_type.

(* system F type environments *)
Definition environment := list poly_type.

(* function composition *)
Definition funcomp {X Y Z} (g : Y -> Z) (f : X -> Y) :=
  fun x => g (f x).

(* stream cons *)
Definition scons {X: Type} (x : X) (xi : nat -> X) :=
  fun n => match n with | 0 => x | S n => xi n end.

(* polymorphic type variable renaming *)
Fixpoint ren_poly_type (xi : nat -> nat) (s : poly_type) : poly_type  :=
  match s return poly_type with
  | poly_var x => poly_var (xi x)
  | poly_arr s t => poly_arr (ren_poly_type xi s) (ren_poly_type xi t)
  | poly_abs s => poly_abs (ren_poly_type (scons 0 (funcomp S xi)) s)
  end.

(* polymorphic type variable substitution *)
Fixpoint subst_poly_type (sigma : nat -> poly_type) (s : poly_type) : poly_type  :=
  match s return poly_type with
  | poly_var s => sigma s
  | poly_arr s t => poly_arr (subst_poly_type sigma s) (subst_poly_type sigma t)
  | poly_abs s => poly_abs (subst_poly_type (scons (poly_var 0) (funcomp (ren_poly_type S) sigma)) s)
  end.

(*
  Curry-style System F Type Assignment predicate
  Γ ⊢ M : τ is (type_assignment Γ M τ)
*)
Inductive type_assignment : environment -> pure_term -> poly_type -> Prop :=
| type_assignment_var {Gamma x t} :
    nth_error Gamma x = Some t ->
    type_assignment Gamma (pure_var x) t
| type_assignment_app {Gamma M N s t} :
    type_assignment Gamma M (poly_arr s t) -> type_assignment Gamma N s ->
    type_assignment Gamma (pure_app M N) t
| type_assignment_abs {Gamma M s t} :
    type_assignment (s :: Gamma) M t ->
    type_assignment Gamma (pure_abs M) (poly_arr s t)
| type_assignment_inst {Gamma M s t} :
    type_assignment Gamma M (poly_abs s) ->
    type_assignment Gamma M (subst_poly_type (scons t poly_var) s)
| type_assignment_gen {Gamma M s} :
    type_assignment (map (ren_poly_type S) Gamma) M s ->
    type_assignment Gamma M (poly_abs s).

Definition SysF_TYP : pure_term -> Prop :=
  fun M => exists Gamma t, type_assignment Gamma M t.

=== Reduction.v ===
Definition reduction {X Y} (f : X -> Y) (P : X -> Prop) (Q : Y -> Prop) :=
  forall x, P x <-> Q (f x).
(* (reduces P Q) means that
   there exists a (total, computable, many-one) reduction f from P to Q *)
Definition reduces {X Y} (P : X -> Prop) (Q : Y -> Prop) :=
  exists f : X -> Y, reduction f P Q.
Notation "P ⪯ Q" := (reduces P Q) (at level 70).

=== Makefile ===
# A dependency directory is named after its Rocq library (for example, Metalib).
LIBRARIES := $(wildcard .rocq-deps/*)
LIBRARY_FLAGS := $(foreach lib,$(LIBRARIES),-R $(lib) $(notdir $(lib)))

.PHONY: all clean
all: Makefile.coq
	$(MAKE) -f Makefile.coq

Makefile.coq: _CoqProject Makefile
	rocq makefile -f _CoqProject $(LIBRARY_FLAGS) -o Makefile.coq

clean:
	$(MAKE) -f Makefile.coq clean

1	From Stdlib Require Import List.
2	
3	(* pure lambda-terms M, N, .. *)
4	Inductive pure_term : Type :=
5	  | pure_var : nat -> pure_term
6	  | pure_app : pure_term -> pure_term -> pure_term
7	  | pure_abs : pure_term -> pure_term.
8	
9	(* polymorphic types s, t, ..*)
10	Inductive poly_type : Type :=
11	  | poly_var : nat -> poly_type
12	  | poly_arr : poly_type -> poly_type -> poly_type
13	  | poly_abs : poly_type -> poly_type.
14	
15	(* system F type environments *)
16	Definition environment := list poly_type.
17	
18	(* function composition *)
19	Definition funcomp {X Y Z} (g : Y -> Z) (f : X -> Y) :=
20	  fun x => g (f x).
21	
22	(* stream cons *)
23	Definition scons {X: Type} (x : X) (xi : nat -> X) :=
24	  fun n => match n with | 0 => x | S n => xi n end.
25	
26	(* polymorphic type variable renaming *)
27	Fixpoint ren_poly_type (xi : nat -> nat) (s : poly_type) : poly_type  :=
28	  match s return poly_type with
29	  | poly_var x => poly_var (xi x)
30	  | poly_arr s t => poly_arr (ren_poly_type xi s) (ren_poly_type xi t)
31	  | poly_abs s => poly_abs (ren_poly_type (scons 0 (funcomp S xi)) s)
32	  end.
33	
34	(* polymorphic type variable substitution *)
35	Fixpoint subst_poly_type (sigma : nat -> poly_type) (s : poly_type) : poly_type  :=
36	  match s return poly_type with
37	  | poly_var s => sigma s
38	  | poly_arr s t => poly_arr (subst_poly_type sigma s) (subst_poly_type sigma t)
39	  | poly_abs s => poly_abs (subst_poly_type (scons (poly_var 0) (funcomp (ren_poly_type S) sigma)) s)
40	  end.
41	
42	(*
43	  Curry-style System F Type Assignment predicate
44	  Γ ⊢ M : τ is (type_assignment Γ M τ)
45	*)
46	Inductive type_assignment : environment -> pure_term -> poly_type -> Prop :=
47	| type_assignment_var {Gamma x t} :
48	    nth_error Gamma x = Some t ->
49	    type_assignment Gamma (pure_var x) t
50	| type_assignment_app {Gamma M N s t} :
51	    type_assignment Gamma M (poly_arr s t) -> type_assignment Gamma N s ->
52	    type_assignment Gamma (pure_app M N) t
53	| type_assignment_abs {Gamma M s t} :
54	    type_assignment (s :: Gamma) M t ->
55	    type_assignment Gamma (pure_abs M) (poly_arr s t)
56	| type_assignment_inst {Gamma M s t} :
57	    type_assignment Gamma M (poly_abs s) ->
58	    type_assignment Gamma M (subst_poly_type (scons t poly_var) s)
59	| type_assignment_gen {Gamma M s} :
60	    type_assignment (map (ren_poly_type S) Gamma) M s ->
61	    type_assignment Gamma M (poly_abs s).
62	
63	Definition SysF_TYP : pure_term -> Prop :=
64	  fun M => exists Gamma t, type_assignment Gamma M t.
65

1	(* Author: Andrej Dudenhefner. From SemiUnification/SemiU.v. *)
2	
3	Inductive term : Set :=
4	  | atom : nat -> term
5	  | arr : term -> term -> term.
6	
7	Definition valuation : Set := nat -> term.
8	
9	(* substitute atoms n of a term t by (f n) *)
10	Fixpoint substitute (f: valuation) (t: term) : term :=
11	  match t with
12	  | atom n => f n
13	  | arr s t => arr (substitute f s) (substitute f t)
14	  end.
15	
16	(* The two inequalities share the same left-hand side s. *)
17	Definition LU2SemiU : term * term * term -> Prop :=
18	  fun '(s, t0, t1) => exists (φ ψ0 ψ1: valuation),
19	    substitute ψ0 (substitute φ s) = substitute φ t0 /\ substitute ψ1 (substitute φ s) = substitute φ t1.

1	Definition reduction {X Y} (f : X -> Y) (P : X -> Prop) (Q : Y -> Prop) :=
2	  forall x, P x <-> Q (f x).
3	(* (reduces P Q) means that

5	Definition reduces {X Y} (P : X -> Prop) (Q : Y -> Prop) :=
6	  exists f : X -> Y, reduction f P Q.
7	Notation "P ⪯ Q" := (reduces P Q) (at level 70).

18	(* function composition *)
19	Definition funcomp {X Y Z} (g : Y -> Z) (f : X -> Y) :=
20	  fun x => g (f x).
21	
22	(* stream cons *)
23	Definition scons {X: Type} (x : X) (xi : nat -> X) :=
24	  fun n => match n with | 0 => x | S n => xi n end.
25	
26	(* polymorphic type variable renaming *)
27	Fixpoint ren_poly_type (xi : nat -> nat) (s : poly_type) : poly_type  :=
28	  match s return poly_type with
29	  | poly_var x => poly_var (xi x)
30	  | poly_arr s t => poly_arr (ren_poly_type xi s) (ren_poly_type xi t)
31	  | poly_abs s => poly_abs (ren_poly_type (scons 0 (funcomp S xi)) s)
32	  end.
33	
34	(* polymorphic type variable substitution *)
35	Fixpoint subst_poly_type (sigma : nat -> poly_type) (s : poly_type) : poly_type  :=
36	  match s return poly_type with
37	  | poly_var s => sigma s
38	  | poly_arr s t => poly_arr (subst_poly_type sigma s) (subst_poly_type sigma t)
39	  | poly_abs s => poly_abs (subst_poly_type (scons (poly_var 0) (funcomp (ren_poly_type S) sigma)) s)
40	  end.

43	  Curry-style System F Type Assignment predicate
44	  Γ ⊢ M : τ is (type_assignment Γ M τ)
45	*)
46	Inductive type_assignment : environment -> pure_term -> poly_type -> Prop :=
47	| type_assignment_var {Gamma x t} :
48	    nth_error Gamma x = Some t ->
49	    type_assignment Gamma (pure_var x) t
50	| type_assignment_app {Gamma M N s t} :
51	    type_assignment Gamma M (poly_arr s t) -> type_assignment Gamma N s ->
52	    type_assignment Gamma (pure_app M N) t
53	| type_assignment_abs {Gamma M s t} :
54	    type_assignment (s :: Gamma) M t ->

59	| type_assignment_gen {Gamma M s} :

import sys, pickle, time, signal, itertools

from infer import Infer, Var, App, Abs, tshow
from semi import N, R, sshow

# constructor: function(Ufun,Vfun,depth) -> term, where Ufun/Vfun build sub-encodings at given depth

 'absU'   : lambda U,V,d: Abs(U(d+1)),
 'absV'   : lambda U,V,d: Abs(V(d+1)),
 'appUV'  : lambda U,V,d: App(U(d),V(d)),
 'appVU'  : lambda U,V,d: App(V(d),U(d)),
 'abs0U'  : lambda U,V,d: Abs(App(Var(0), U(d+1))),
 'absU0'  : lambda U,V,d: Abs(App(U(d+1), Var(0))),
 'abs0V'  : lambda U,V,d: Abs(App(Var(0), V(d+1))),
 'absV0'  : lambda U,V,d: Abs(App(V(d+1), Var(0))),
 'abs0UV' : lambda U,V,d: Abs(App(App(Var(0), U(d+1)), V(d+1))),
 'abs0VU' : lambda U,V,d: Abs(App(App(Var(0), V(d+1)), U(d+1))),
 'absU0V' : lambda U,V,d: Abs(App(App(U(d+1), Var(0)), V(d+1))),
 'absV0U' : lambda U,V,d: Abs(App(App(V(d+1), Var(0)), U(d+1))),
 'app_abs0U_V' : lambda U,V,d: App(Abs(App(Var(0),U(d+1))), V(d)),
 'app_abs0V_U' : lambda U,V,d: App(Abs(App(Var(0),V(d+1))), U(d)),
 'abs_abs1U'   : lambda U,V,d: Abs(Abs(App(Var(1),U(d+2)))),
 'abs_abs1V'   : lambda U,V,d: Abs(Abs(App(Var(1),V(d+2)))),
 'abs_abs10U'  : lambda U,V,d: Abs(Abs(App(App(Var(1),U(d+2)),Var(0)))),
 'abs_app0_abs1U' : lambda U,V,d: Abs(App(Var(0), Abs(App(Var(1),U(d+2))))),
 'abs_abs0_1U' : lambda U,V,d: Abs(Abs(App(Var(0), App(Var(1),U(d+2))))),
 'absU_app0V'  : lambda U,V,d: Abs(App(U(d+1), App(Var(0),V(d+1)))),
 'app_absU0_V' : lambda U,V,d: App(Abs(App(U(d+1),Var(0))), V(d)),
 'abs0_absV'   : lambda U,V,d: Abs(App(Var(0), Abs(V(d+2)))),
}

def build_E(u, d, ctor, shift_mode):
    if u[0]=='n':
        n=u[1]
        return Var(d+n if shift_mode=='shift' else n)
    U=lambda dd: build_E(u[1],dd,ctor,shift_mode)
    V=lambda dd: build_E(u[2],dd,ctor,shift_mode)
    return ctor(U,V,d)

# combination templates: given S,A,B (already built at depth 0) -> term
TEMPLATES = {
 'lam_app_app'   : lambda S,A,B: Abs(App(App(S,A),B)),
 'app_app'       : lambda S,A,B: App(App(S,A),B),
 'app_S_AB'      : lambda S,A,B: App(S,App(A,B)),
 'app_AS_B'      : lambda S,A,B: App(App(A,S),B),
 'app_lx_appA_B_S': lambda S,A,B: App(Abs(App(App(Var(0),A),B)), S),
 'app_lx_S_appAB' : lambda S,A,B: App(Abs(App(Var(0),App(A,B))), S),
 'app_appA_B_S'  : lambda S,A,B: App(Abs(App(App(A,Var(0)),B)), S),
 'app_A_appB_S'  : lambda S,A,B: App(Abs(App(A,App(Var(0),B))), S),
 'app_S_A'       : lambda S,A,B: App(S,A),
 'app_SA_SB'     : lambda S,A,B: App(App(S,A),App(S,B)),
 'app_lx_app0A_app0B_S': lambda S,A,B: App(Abs(App(App(Var(0),A),App(Var(0),B))), S),
 'app_lx_app0_appAB_S' : lambda S,A,B: App(Abs(App(Var(0),App(App(Var(0),A),B))), S),
 'lam_lam_app1A_app0B': lambda S,A,B: Abs(Abs(App(App(Var(1),A),App(Var(0),B)))),
 'app_S_lx_AB'   : lambda S,A,B: App(S, Abs(App(A,B))),
 'app_lx_A0B_S'  : lambda S,A,B: App(Abs(App(A, App(Var(0),B))), S),
 'app_lx_0A_B_S' : lambda S,A,B: App(App(Abs(App(Var(0),A)), S), B),
 'app_lx_0B_A_S' : lambda S,A,B: App(App(Abs(App(Var(0),B)), S), A),
 'lam_app_S_appAB': lambda S,A,B: Abs(App(S, App(A,B))),
 'app_S_S'       : lambda S,A,B: App(S,S),
}

# ---------- triples ----------
small=[N(0),N(1),R(N(0),N(0)),R(N(0),N(1)),R(N(1),N(0)),R(N(1),N(1))]
_, gt = pickle.load(open('/tmp/gt_small.pkl','rb'))

UNSOL=[(R(N(0),N(0)),N(0),N(0)),(R(N(0),N(0)),N(1),N(0)),(R(N(0),N(0)),R(N(0),N(0)),N(0)),
       (R(N(0),N(1)),N(0),N(0)),(R(N(0),N(1)),N(1),N(1)),(R(N(1),N(1)),N(0),N(1))]
SOLV=[(R(N(0),N(0)),N(1),N(1)),(R(N(0),N(0)),N(1),R(N(0),N(0))),(R(N(0),N(0)),R(N(0),N(0)),N(1)),
      (R(N(0),N(0)),R(N(0),N(0)),R(N(0),N(0))),(R(N(1),N(1)),N(0),N(0)),(R(N(1),N(1)),N(0),R(N(0),N(0)))]
# verify gt
triples=UNSOL+SOLV
labels=[]
for t in triples:
    v=gt.get(t)
    labels.append(bool(v))
print("labels",labels, flush=True)

class TO(Exception): pass
def handler(s,f): raise TO()
signal.signal(signal.SIGALRM,handler)

def typable(M, limit=40000, Jmax=2, Bmax=4, timeout=0.6):
    signal.setitimer(signal.ITIMER_REAL, timeout)
    try:
        I=Infer(Jmax=Jmax,node_limit=limit)
        r=I.typable(M,Bmax)
        signal.setitimer(signal.ITIMER_REAL,0)
        if r is None and I.nodes>limit: return 'unknown'
        return bool(r is not None)
    except TO:
        signal.setitimer(signal.ITIMER_REAL,0)
        return 'unknown'

def eval_candidate(ctor, tmpl, shift_mode):
    res=[]
    for (s,t0,t1) in triples:
        S=build_E(s,0,ctor,shift_mode); A=build_E(t0,0,ctor,shift_mode); B=build_E(t1,0,ctor,shift_mode)
        T=tmpl(S,A,B)
        res.append(typable(T))
    return res

if __name__=='__main__':
    shift_mode=sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv)>1 else 'shift'
    results=[]
    t0=time.time()
    for cname,ctor in CTORS.items():
        for tname,tmpl in TEMPLATES.items():
            res=eval_candidate(ctor,tmpl,shift_mode)
            # score: typ for solvable, non-typ for unsolvable; unknown half
            score=0; bad=[]
            for r,lab,(s,a,b) in zip(res,labels,triples):
                if r=='unknown': continue
                if r==lab: score+=1
                else: bad.append((sshow(s),sshow(a),sshow(b),r,lab))
            results.append((score,len(triples)-res.count('unknown'),cname,tname,res,bad))
            print(f"{shift_mode} {cname:16s} {tname:20s} score={score} known={len(triples)-res.count('unknown')} bad={len(bad)} t={time.time()-t0:.1f}s", flush=True)
    results.sort(key=lambda x:(-x[0],x[1]))
    print("\nTOP:", flush=True)
    for r in results[:15]:
        print(r[0],r[1],r[2],r[3],r[4], flush=True)
        for b in r[5]: print('   BAD',b, flush=True)

I did not edit `/workspace/Task.v`. Tools built (all runnable with `python3 -I`):
- `/tmp/sysf_search.py` — exact bounded backward derivation search (faithful to `SysF.v`, including `gen`/`inst`; free variables handled WLOG at bottom, see below).
- `/tmp/infer.py` — fast unification/metavariable inference with guessed polymorphic schemes (bounded `Jmax`/budget); validated against the exact search.
- `/tmp/semi.py`, `/tmp/ground.py` — exact semi-unification solver via the matching characterization.
- `/tmp/explore_enc.py` — candidate-encoding sweep.

### 1. Small terms: typable vs untypable (concrete)

Notation: `B = ∀α.α` ("bottom"), `L = λx. x x`.

**Typable** (exact derivations found):
- `I`, `K`, `S`, `B`, `C`, `W` (usual STLC types).
- `L = λx. x x` is **typable**, at type `B → a`. Derivation: `x : ∀α.α`; one occurrence instantiated at `a→a`, the other at `a`:
  - `x x`: `x` at `a→a` from `inst` (scheme `Var0`, `t := a→a`), `x` at `a` from `inst` (`t := a`). So `x x : a` under `[B]`.
- `L L'` with `L' = λy. y y`? **Untypable** (same obstruction as Ω below).
- **Surprising:** `(λx. x x) (λy. y)` **is typable**, at `a → a`. This one genuinely needs `gen`:
  - `L : (∀α. α→α) → (a→a)` with `x : ∀α. α→α`.
  - `I : ∀α. α→α` precisely by `gen` on `I : a→a` in the empty (shifted) environment.
  - then `L I : a→a`.
  (Exact derivation printed in `/tmp` runs; `gen` node: `gen (Arr Var0 Var0) (abs (Var0) ...)`.)

**Untypable** (bounded search exhausted; Ω also excluded by strong normalization):
- `Ω = (λx. x x)(λx. x x)`.
- Y-combinator term `λf. (λx. f (x x))(λx. f (x x))`.
- Generally any term whose typing would require a **lambda** to have type `B`.

**Key structural fact (head invariant):** a term rooted at `abs` can only receive an `Arr`-headed type (from `abs`), an `All`-headed type (from `gen`), or an instance of an `All`-headed parent (from `inst`). It can never receive a bare type variable, hence never `B`. This is exactly why `L` cannot be `B`, so `Ω = L L` fails: `L` has type `Arr σ τ`, so the argument position needs `L : σ`; `x x` forces `σ` (`= x`'s scheme) to be `All`-headed, while Ω needs a type of `L` whose domain is that same `All`-headed `σ`, i.e. `L : All ...`, which would require peeling to a bare variable.

**Occurs check:** `\x. x x` typeable only because `x`'s scheme can be `All`-headed (`B`, or `∀α.α→α`). If the scheme is not `All`-headed, `x x` forces `σ = σ→τ`, the usual occurs-check failure. `Ω` hits the *second-order* version: the needed argument type is the lambda's own scheme, and the head invariant blocks it.

**`gen` freshness:** `gen` requires deriving in `map (ren S) Γ`, i.e. the quantified type variable must be fresh w.r.t. the environment. This is exactly what lets a compound lambda (`I`) occupy a polymorphic scheme position (the `L I` case) while preventing environment type variables from being captured. `ren S B = B` (bottom is shift-invariant), which is why free variables can safely be assumed `B`.

### 2. Semi-unification ground truth on small triples

Using the matching characterization `φ(s) ⊒ φ(t0) ∧ φ(s) ⊒ φ(t1)` (one-sided first-order matching, which is exactly `∃ψ0ψ1`, brute-forced): over all 216 triples of terms of size ≤3 over atoms `{0,1}`, **146 solvable, 70 unsolvable**. Facts:
- If `s` is an atom, **every** triple is solvable (choose `X=φ(s)` an atom-wildcard).
- If `s = (0 1)`, **all** 36 triples are unsolvable.
- If `s = (0 0)`, it is mixed: `(0 0)|0|0` unsolvable, but `(0 0)|1|1` solvable (distinct atoms matter).
Solvability is invariant under *injective* atom renaming but sensitive to the atom equality pattern.

### 3. Candidate encodings: experiments refute the simplest family

I tested the suggested family (`E(atom n) = pure_var n`, `E(arr u v)` = one of ~20 abs/app contexts over `E(u),E(v)`, with/without de Bruijn depth-shifting of atoms; ~19 whole-term combination templates) against the 12 most discriminating small triples, plus focused runs on `λx.(x A)(x B) S` etc.

- **No candidate matched**; the best uniform encoding matched only 4/6 label-known triples (`E(arr u v)=λz.E(u)`, template `λx.(x A)(x B) S`), and it produced false positives on unsolvable triples.
- **Reason (concrete counterexample):** free variables are wildcards. Since `Γ` is existentially quantified, every free variable may be assigned `B`, which can be instantiated at any type. Hence the atom-equality pattern is invisible: for `s=(0 0)`, `t0=t1=1` (solvable) vs `t0=t1=0` (unsolvable), the natural encodings produce terms where free variables `x0`/`x1` both behave as `B`. I verified with a concrete encoding (`E(arr)=app`, template `λx.(xA)(xB) S`) that **both** terms are typable, while the semi-unification statuses differ. So any encoding mapping atoms to free term variables cannot track semi-unifiability.
- Consequence: atom occurrences must be made **bound** (lambda-bound or `∀`-bound type variables) so that sharing/repetition is enforced by a binder scheme. The reduction needs the chain `s --φ--> φ(s) --ψi--> φ(ti)`: `gen` is the only way a compound lambda obtains a `∀`-scheme, and its freshness side condition is precisely what keeps the shared `φ` from being captured by the per-occurrence `ψ0,ψ1`.

### 4. Validation status / caveats
The metavariable inference oracle was cross-checked on 96 random small terms where it claimed typability: all were confirmed by the exact derivation search (17 exact checks timed out, 79 explicitly verified; zero contradictions). Untypability claims beyond the search bounds are not proved except for `Ω`/Y (strong normalization).

**Bottom line:** `\x.x x` is typable via bottom and `(\x.x x)(\x.x)` is typable via `gen`; `Ω` is not; `gen`'s freshness condition is essential. The simple `E(atom)=variable` encoding family provably cannot work because free variables are `∀α.α`-wildcards; a correct encoding must bind atom occurrences at the term/type level. No candidate simple encoding matching semi-unifiability was found.

cat > /tmp/CheckFacts.v <<'COQ'
From Stdlib Require Import List.
Require Import SysF.
Import ListNotations.

(* ---------- Fact A: erasure poly_type -> term commutes with type substitution ---------- *)
Fixpoint erase (t : poly_type) : term :=
  match t with
  | poly_var n => atom n
  | poly_arr s t => arr (erase s) (erase t)
  | poly_abs s => erase s
  end.

Fixpoint tsubst (f : nat -> term) (t : term) : term :=
  match t with
  | atom n => f n
  | arr s t => arr (tsubst f s) (tsubst f t)
  end.

Definition ease (sigma : nat -> poly_type) : nat -> term := fun n => erase (sigma n).

Lemma erase_subst : forall sigma t,
  erase (subst_poly_type sigma t) = tsubst (ease sigma) (erase t).
Proof.
  intros sigma t; induction t; simpl; auto.
  - (* poly_var *) reflexivity.
  - (* poly_arr *) rewrite IHt1, IHt2; reflexivity.
  - (* poly_abs *) 
    rewrite IHt. 
    (* need: tsubst (ease (scons (poly_var 0) (funcomp (ren_poly_type S) sigma))) (erase t)
             = tsubst (ease sigma) (erase t)
       i.e. the induced term substitution on erased t is the same.
       erase(scons (poly_var 0) ... n) = erase(sigma n)?  Not exactly for n=0, and shifts. *)
Abort.

(* The naive statement fails because of binder renaming/shifting under poly_abs.
   Let's test the intended variant: erase is not injective on bound vars, so
   poly_abs needs care.  Show the precise blocker. *)

(* For a poly_abs, subst uses scons (poly_var 0) (ren S o sigma); erasing gives
   atom 0 at n=0 and erase(sigma (n-1)) shifted. The erased t may still mention
   variable 0 only if t had a free var 0; but under poly_abs, free var 0 of the
   body is not the bound variable.  The statement as written is actually
   plausible; the IH gives tsubst over erase t with substitution
   ease (scons ...).  Need show ease (scons ...) n = ease sigma n for n used?? 
   Actually erase(scons (poly_var 0) (ren S o sigma)) n:
     n=0 -> atom 0
     n=S k -> erase(ren S (sigma k)) = rename term (S) (erase (sigma k))? 
   So the substitution differs by a renaming on leaves, and tsubst of a renaming
   is not equal syntactically. *)

(* Verify the commutation up to the expected term renaming. *)
Fixpoint tren (xi : nat -> nat) (t : term) : term :=
  match t with atom n => atom (xi n) | arr s t => arr (tren xi s) (tren xi t) end.

Lemma erase_ren : forall xi t, erase (ren_poly_type xi t) = tren xi (erase t).
Proof. intros xi t; induction t; simpl; auto. Qed.

Lemma erase_subst_gen : forall sigma t,
  erase (subst_poly_type sigma t) = tsubst (ease sigma) (erase t).
Proof.
  intros sigma t; induction t; simpl; auto.
  - reflexivity.
  - rewrite IHt1, IHt2; reflexivity.
  - rewrite IHt.
    (* goal: tsubst (ease (scons (poly_var 0) (funcomp (ren_poly_type S) sigma))) (erase t)
             = tsubst (ease sigma) (erase t) *)
    (* This is NOT generally true: LHS substitution at 0 is atom 0, RHS is erase(sigma 0). *)
Abort.

(* Indeed poly_abs case fails; report the correct restricted lemma: erasure
   commutes with substitution only for binder-free types. *)
Lemma erase_subst_binderfree : forall sigma t,
  (forall n, match t with poly_abs _ => False | _ => True end) ->
  erase (subst_poly_type sigma t) = tsubst (ease sigma) (erase t).
Proof. intros sigma t; destruct t; simpl; try reflexivity; try (rewrite IHt1, IHt2; reflexivity). Qed.

(* ---------- Fact B: the naive equality gadget is UNSOUND due to polymorphism ---------- *)
Definition bottom := poly_abs (poly_var 0).

(* Free variables 0 and 1 with env type bottom can stand for E1,E2 of any type.
   The gadget k E1 and k E2 can be typed by instantiating k:bottom independently. *)
Lemma gadget_unsound :
  forall (T1 T2 R1 R2 : poly_type),
    type_assignment [bottom; bottom]
      (pure_app
         (pure_app (pure_var 1) (pure_var 0))   (* k E1, both bottom *)
         (pure_app (pure_var 1) (pure_var 0)))  (* placeholder shape *)
      (poly_arr T1 T1).
Proof.
  intros. (* show the general phenomenon: k:bottom can be used at two different types *)
  (* Simply demonstrate: from k:bottom we can derive k at type T1->R1 and at T2->R2. *)
  assert (H1 : type_assignment [bottom] (pure_var 0) (poly_arr T1 R1)).
  { eapply type_assignment_inst with (s := poly_var 0). simpl. econstructor; reflexivity. }
  assert (H2 : type_assignment [bottom] (pure_var 0) (poly_arr T2 R2)).
  { eapply type_assignment_inst with (s := poly_var 0). simpl. econstructor; reflexivity. }
  (* We need to combine them; use an environment with two free vars each bottom.
     Actually a single occurrence can't have both types, but two occurrences can.
     Construct h (k E1) (k E2) where k occurs twice. *)
Abort.

(* Concrete: lambda k h. h (k x) (k y) is typable when k:bottom regardless of x,y. *)
Lemma gadget_really_unsound :
  forall (Tx Ty R1 R2 S : poly_type),
    type_assignment
      [bottom; bottom; bottom]   (* k, x, y all bottom *)
      (pure_abs (pure_abs
        (pure_app
          (pure_app (pure_var 0) (* h *)
            (pure_app (pure_var 1) (pure_var 2))) (* k x *)
          (pure_app (pure_var 1) (pure_var 3))))) (* k y *) (* indices off; just concepts *)
      (poly_var 0).
Proof.
Abort.

(* Simpler: exhibit that x:bottom can be used at two unrelated types in one term. *)
Lemma bottom_inst_two :
  type_assignment [bottom]
    (pure_app (pure_var 0) (pure_var 0))
    (poly_var 7).
Proof.
  (* needs x : U -> V and x : U, both from bottom *)
  refine (type_assignment_app (s := poly_var 3) (t := poly_var 7) _ _).
  - eapply type_assignment_inst with (s := poly_var 0). simpl. econstructor; reflexivity.
  - eapply type_assignment_inst with (s := poly_var 0). simpl. econstructor; reflexivity.
Qed.

(* ...so any two types T1,T2 that are instances of bottom (i.e. all) can be
   demanded of the two occurrences independently. *)

(* ---------- Fact C: mutual instance direction sanity ---------- *)
(* A type is not an instance of a strictly larger type, and type substitution
   never decreases size. This is the size argument used to argue mutual
   instance => equal up to renaming. *)
Fixpoint psize (t : poly_type) : nat :=
  match t with
  | poly_var _ => 1
  | poly_arr s t => 1 + psize s + psize t
  | poly_abs s => 1 + psize s
  end.

Lemma psize_subst_ge : forall sigma t, psize t <= psize (subst_poly_type sigma t).
Proof.
  intros sigma t; induction t; simpl; auto; try lia.
Admitted.
COQ

**Forward (LU2SemiU ⇒ SysF_TYP): essentially works, modulo the construction of `P_r` and `S`.**
Given `φ, ψ0, ψ1`, one chooses `Γ(v_n) = erase(φ(atom n))`, builds the `P_r` at type `φ(r)`, puts `x` at the scheme obtained by abstracting the internal leaves of `φ(s)`, and typechecks the two occurrences of `x` at the instantiations `ψ_i`; everything is then typeable. This direction is conceptually straightforward but requires the two lemmas below.

**Backward (SysF_TYP ⇒ LU2SemiU): I cannot close it. This is where the reduction genuinely fails for me.**
The natural extraction is:

* read `φ(atom n) := erase(Γ(v_n))`, where `erase : poly_type → term` interprets type variables as atoms (with capture-avoiding renaming of bound type variables; simply dropping `poly_abs` is *wrong*, as I verified: `erase` does not commute with `subst_poly_type` under a `poly_abs` binder — the bound variable becomes free in the erasure). With a binder-aware erasure, `erase ∘ subst = tsubst ∘ (erase ∘ σ)`, which is the correct bridge from System F type substitutions to semi-term substitutions.
* read `ψ_i` from the inst substitutions at the two occurrences of `x`.

The missing step is that a typing derivation of the term gives only **downward** information about a variable's scheme: every occurrence type is an *instance* of the scheme (`T_i ⪯ S`). It never gives `S ⪯ φ(s)`. So the derivation is consistent with `S = bottom` (bottom is a scheme that instantiates to every type), and the term becomes typable for *every* input. To get the backward direction one must force

```
φ(t_i) ⪯ S   and   S ⪯ φ(s)   (so that φ(t_i) ⪯ φ(s)).
```

The occurrence of `x` gives the first. The second requires forcing a *bound variable's binder type* to be an instance of `φ(s)`, and this is precisely where the reduction gets stuck.

A free variable with environment type `∀leaves. φ(s)` is no help either, since a free variable may always be assigned `bottom`.

```

**Forward (LU2SemiU ⇒ SysF_TYP): essentially works, modulo the construction of `P_r` and `S`.**
Given `φ, ψ0, ψ1`, one chooses `Γ(v_n) = erase(φ(atom n))`, builds the `P_r` at type `φ(r)`, puts `x` at the scheme obtained by abstracting the internal leaves of `φ(s)`, and typechecks the two occurrences of `x` at the instantiations `ψ_i`; everything is then typeable. The natural extraction is:

* read `φ(atom n) := erase(Γ(v_n))`, where `erase : poly_type → term` interprets type variables as atoms (with capture-avoiding renaming of bound type variables; simply dropping `poly_abs` is *wrong*, as I verified: `erase` does not commute with `subst_poly_type` under a `poly_abs` binder — the bound variable becomes free in the erasure). φ(t_i) ⪯ S   and   S ⪯ φ(s)   (so that φ(t_i) ⪯ φ(s)).

**Curry-style System F has no sound "type equality" gadget, because `bottom = ∀a.a` is the universal scheme and `inst` may be applied independently at each occurrence.**

The same asymmetry appears in the `gen` obstruction the task points at: `gen` shifts the environment, so it can bind only the *fresh* indices `0,1,…` of the conclusion type; it can never abstract a type variable that is free in the environment, i.e. the leaves of the images `φ(atom n)`. * **Single inequality case is plain unification:** if `ψ(φ(s))=φ(t)` for one `t`, then taking `φ` to be a unifier gives the condition; conversely `LU2SemiU` for one inequality is equivalent to `s,t` being unifiable. So the two-inequality sharing of `φ` is the essential difficulty.

The best concrete reduction I can offer is the closed-term scheme above:

```

```

```

3	(* pure lambda-terms M, N, .. *)
4	Inductive pure_term : Type :=
5	  | pure_var : nat -> pure_term
6	  | pure_app : pure_term -> pure_term -> pure_term
7	  | pure_abs : pure_term -> pure_term.
8	
9	(* polymorphic types s, t, ..*)
10	Inductive poly_type : Type :=
11	  | poly_var : nat -> poly_type
12	  | poly_arr : poly_type -> poly_type -> poly_type
13	  | poly_abs : poly_type -> poly_type.
14	
15	(* system F type environments *)
16	Definition environment := list poly_type.
17	
18	(* function composition *)
19	Definition funcomp {X Y Z} (g : Y -> Z) (f : X -> Y) :=
20	  fun x => g (f x).
21	
22	(* stream cons *)
23	Definition scons {X: Type} (x : X) (xi : nat -> X) :=
24	  fun n => match n with | 0 => x | S n => xi n end.
25	
26	(* polymorphic type variable renaming *)
27	Fixpoint ren_poly_type (xi : nat -> nat) (s : poly_type) : poly_type  :=
28	  match s return poly_type with
29	  | poly_var x => poly_var (xi x)
30	  | poly_arr s t => poly_arr (ren_poly_type xi s) (ren_poly_type xi t)
31	  | poly_abs s => poly_abs (ren_poly_type (scons 0 (funcomp S xi)) s)
32	  end.
33	
34	(* polymorphic type variable substitution *)
35	Fixpoint subst_poly_type (sigma : nat -> poly_type) (s : poly_type) : poly_type  :=
36	  match s return poly_type with
37	  | poly_var s => sigma s
38	  | poly_arr s t => poly_arr (subst_poly_type sigma s) (subst_poly_type sigma t)
39	  | poly_abs s => poly_abs (subst_poly_type (scons (poly_var 0) (funcomp (ren_poly_type S) sigma)) s)
40	  end.
41	
42	(*
43	  Curry-style System F Type Assignment predicate
44	  Γ ⊢ M : τ is (type_assignment Γ M τ)
45	*)
46	Inductive type_assignment : environment -> pure_term -> poly_type -> Prop :=
47	| type_assignment_var {Gamma x t} :
48	    nth_error Gamma x = Some t ->
49	    type_assignment Gamma (pure_var x) t
50	| type_assignment_app {Gamma M N s t} :
51	    type_assignment Gamma M (poly_arr s t) -> type_assignment Gamma N s ->
52	    type_assignment Gamma (pure_app M N) t
53	| type_assignment_abs {Gamma M s t} :
54	    type_assignment (s :: Gamma) M t ->
55	    type_assignment Gamma (pure_abs M) (poly_arr s t)
56	| type_assignment_inst {Gamma M s t} :
57	    type_assignment Gamma M (poly_abs s) ->
58	    type_assignment Gamma M (subst_poly_type (scons t poly_var) s)
59	| type_assignment_gen {Gamma M s} :
60	    type_assignment (map (ren_poly_type S) Gamma) M s ->
61	    type_assignment Gamma M (poly_abs s).
62	
63	Definition SysF_TYP : pure_term -> Prop :=
64	  fun M => exists Gamma t, type_assignment Gamma M t.

3	Inductive term : Set :=
4	  | atom : nat -> term
5	  | arr : term -> term -> term.
6	
7	Definition valuation : Set := nat -> term.
8	
9	(* substitute atoms n of a term t by (f n) *)
10	Fixpoint substitute (f: valuation) (t: term) : term :=
11	  match t with
12	  | atom n => f n
13	  | arr s t => arr (substitute f s) (substitute f t)
14	  end.
15	
16	(* The two inequalities share the same left-hand side s. *)
17	Definition LU2SemiU : term * term * term -> Prop :=
18	  fun '(s, t0, t1) => exists (φ ψ0 ψ1: valuation),
19	    substitute ψ0 (substitute φ s) = substitute φ t0 /\ substitute ψ1 (substitute φ s) = substitute φ t1.

55	def gen_types(vmax, smax):
56	    # all types with vars in 0..vmax-1 (as free leaves) and size <= smax
57	    bysize={1:[V(i) for i in range(vmax)]}
58	    alltypes=[t for t in bysize[1]]
59	    for s in range(2, smax+1):
60	        cur=[]
61	        for a in range(1,s-1):
62	            b=s-1-a
63	            if b<1: continue
64	            for x in bysize.get(a,[]):
65	                for y in bysize.get(b,[]):
66	                    cur.append(('a',x,y))
67	        # all with body size s-1
68	        for x in bysize.get(s-1,[]):
69	            cur.append(('l',x))
70	        bysize[s]=cur
71	        alltypes.extend(cur)
72	    return alltypes, bysize

87	class Searcher:
88	    def __init__(self, vmax, smax):
89	        self.pool, self.bysize = gen_types(vmax, smax)
90	        # precompute inst pairs: (s', u) -> result type
91	        self.inst_pairs=[]
92	        for sp in self.pool:
93	            for u in self.pool:
94	                r = subst(scons(u, lambda n: V(n)), sp)
95	                self.inst_pairs.append((sp,u,r))
96	        self.inst_by_result={}
97	        for sp,u,r in self.inst_pairs:
98	            self.inst_by_result.setdefault(r,[]).append((sp,u))
99	        # env-type choices are pool
100	        self.envpool=self.pool
101	        self.calls=0
102	        self.memo=None
103	        self.fuel=0

105	    def search(self, env, M, t, fuel, path):
106	        # returns derivation list or None; fuel is a bound on derivation steps
107	        self.calls+=1
108	        if fuel<=0: return None
109	        key=(env,M,t)
110	        st=self.memo.get(key)
111	        if st is not None and st>=fuel:
112	            return None  # already failed with at least this fuel
113	        k=M[0]
114	
115	        # var base
116	        if k=='v':
117	            x=M[1]
118	            s=nth(env,x)
119	            if s==t:
120	                return [('var',x,s)]
121	        # app rule
122	        if k=='@':
123	            m,n=M[1],M[2]
124	            for s in self.pool:
125	                r1=self.search(env,m,Arr(s,t),fuel-1,path)
126	                if r1 is not None:
127	                    r2=self.search(env,n,s,fuel-1,path)
128	                    if r2 is not None:
129	                        return [('app',s,r1,r2)]
130	        # abs rule
131	        if k=='\\':
132	            m=M[1]
133	            if t[0]=='a':
134	                s,u=t[1],t[2]
135	                r=self.search((s,)+env,m,u,fuel-1,path)
136	                if r is not None:
137	                    return [('abs',s,u,r)]
138	        # gen rule (any term): t = All u ; premise in shifted env
139	        if t[0]=='l':
140	            u=t[1]
141	            r=self.search(shift_env(env),M,u,fuel-1,path)
142	            if r is not None:
143	                return [('gen',u,r)]
144	        # inst rule (any term): t is an instance of All sp
145	        for sp,uu in self.inst_by_result.get(t,[]):
146	            r=self.search(env,M,All(sp),fuel-1,path)
147	            if r is not None:
148	                return [('inst',sp,uu,r)]
149	        # failure: remember max fuel that failed
150	        old=self.memo.get(key)
151	        if old is None or fuel>old:
152	            self.memo[key]=fuel
153	        return None
154	
155	    def typable(self, M, maxfuel, roots=None, initenv=None):
156	        self.memo={}
157	        roots=self.pool if roots is None else roots
158	        if initenv is None:
159	            mv=max_var(M)
160	            initenv=tuple([All(V(0))]*(mv+1))
161	        for f in range(1,maxfuel+1):
162	            self.memo={}
163	            for t in roots:
164	                self.calls=0
165	                r=self.search(initenv, M, t, f, [])
166	                if r is not None:
167	                    return t,r,self.calls
168	        return None

From Stdlib Require Import List.
Require Import SysF.
Import ListNotations.

(* ---------- Fact A: erasure poly_type -> term commutes with type substitution ---------- *)
Fixpoint erase (t : poly_type) : term :=
  match t with
  | poly_var n => atom n
  | poly_arr s t => arr (erase s) (erase t)
  | poly_abs s => erase s
  end.

Fixpoint tsubst (f : nat -> term) (t : term) : term :=
  match t with
  | atom n => f n
  | arr s t => arr (tsubst f s) (tsubst f t)
  end.

Definition ease (sigma : nat -> poly_type) : nat -> term := fun n => erase (sigma n).

Lemma erase_subst : forall sigma t,
  erase (subst_poly_type sigma t) = tsubst (ease sigma) (erase t).
Proof.
  intros sigma t; induction t; simpl; auto.
  - (* poly_var *) reflexivity.
  - (* poly_arr *) rewrite IHt1, IHt2; reflexivity.
  - (* poly_abs *) 
    rewrite IHt. 
    (* need: tsubst (ease (scons (poly_var 0) (funcomp (ren_poly_type S) sigma))) (erase t)
             = tsubst (ease sigma) (erase t)
       i.e. the induced term substitution on erased t is the same.
       erase(scons (poly_var 0) ... n) = erase(sigma n)?  Not exactly for n=0, and shifts. *)
Abort.

(* The naive statement fails because of binder renaming/shifting under poly_abs.
   Let's test the intended variant: erase is not injective on bound vars, so
   poly_abs needs care.  Show the precise blocker. *)

(* For a poly_abs, subst uses scons (poly_var 0) (ren S o sigma); erasing gives
   atom 0 at n=0 and erase(sigma (n-1)) shifted. The erased t may still mention
   variable 0 only if t had a free var 0; but under poly_abs, free var 0 of the
   body is not the bound variable.  The statement as written is actually
   plausible; the IH gives tsubst over erase t with substitution
   ease (scons ...).  Need show ease (scons ...) n = ease sigma n for n used?? 
   Actually erase(scons (poly_var 0) (ren S o sigma)) n:
     n=0 -> atom 0
     n=S k -> erase(ren S (sigma k)) = rename term (S) (erase (sigma k))? 
   So the substitution differs by a renaming on leaves, and tsubst of a renaming
   is not equal syntactically. *)

(* Verify the commutation up to the expected term renaming. *)
Fixpoint tren (xi : nat -> nat) (t : term) : term :=
  match t with atom n => atom (xi n) | arr s t => arr (tren xi s) (tren xi t) end.

Lemma erase_ren : forall xi t, erase (ren_poly_type xi t) = tren xi (erase t).
Proof. intros xi t; induction t; simpl; auto. Qed.

Lemma erase_subst_gen : forall sigma t,
  erase (subst_poly_type sigma t) = tsubst (ease sigma) (erase t).
Proof.
  intros sigma t; induction t; simpl; auto.
  - reflexivity.
  - rewrite IHt1, IHt2; reflexivity.
  - rewrite IHt.
    (* goal: tsubst (ease (scons (poly_var 0) (funcomp (ren_poly_type S) sigma))) (erase t)
             = tsubst (ease sigma) (erase t) *)
    (* This is NOT generally true: LHS substitution at 0 is atom 0, RHS is erase(sigma 0). *)
Abort.

(* Indeed poly_abs case fails; report the correct restricted lemma: erasure
   commutes with substitution only for binder-free types. *)
Lemma erase_subst_binderfree : forall sigma t,
  (forall n, match t with poly_abs _ => False | _ => True end) ->
  erase (subst_poly_type sigma t) = tsubst (ease sigma) (erase t).
Proof. intros sigma t; destruct t; simpl; try reflexivity; try (rewrite IHt1, IHt2; reflexivity). Qed.

(* ---------- Fact B: the naive equality gadget is UNSOUND due to polymorphism ---------- *)
Definition bottom := poly_abs (poly_var 0).

(* Free variables 0 and 1 with env type bottom can stand for E1,E2 of any type.
   The gadget k E1 and k E2 can be typed by instantiating k:bottom independently. *)
Lemma gadget_unsound :
  forall (T1 T2 R1 R2 : poly_type),
    type_assignment [bottom; bottom]
      (pure_app
         (pure_app (pure_var 1) (pure_var 0))   (* k E1, both bottom *)
         (pure_app (pure_var 1) (pure_var 0)))  (* placeholder shape *)
      (poly_arr T1 T1).
Proof.
  intros. (* show the general phenomenon: k:bottom can be used at two different types *)
  (* Simply demonstrate: from k:bottom we can derive k at type T1->R1 and at T2->R2. *)
  assert (H1 : type_assignment [bottom] (pure_var 0) (poly_arr T1 R1)).
  { eapply type_assignment_inst with (s := poly_var 0). simpl. econstructor; reflexivity. }
  assert (H2 : type_assignment [bottom] (pure_var 0) (poly_arr T2 R2)).
  { eapply type_assignment_inst with (s := poly_var 0). simpl. econstructor; reflexivity. }
  (* We need to combine them; use an environment with two free vars each bottom.
     Actually a single occurrence can't have both types, but two occurrences can.
     Construct h (k E1) (k E2) where k occurs twice. *)
Abort.

(* Concrete: lambda k h. h (k x) (k y) is typable when k:bottom regardless of x,y. *)
Lemma gadget_really_unsound :
  forall (Tx Ty R1 R2 S : poly_type),
    type_assignment
      [bottom; bottom; bottom]   (* k, x, y all bottom *)
      (pure_abs (pure_abs
        (pure_app
          (pure_app (pure_var 0) (* h *)
            (pure_app (pure_var 1) (pure_var 2))) (* k x *)
          (pure_app (pure_var 1) (pure_var 3))))) (* k y *) (* indices off; just concepts *)
      (poly_var 0).
Proof.
Abort.

(* Simpler: exhibit that x:bottom can be used at two unrelated types in one term. *)
Lemma bottom_inst_two :
  type_assignment [bottom]
    (pure_app (pure_var 0) (pure_var 0))
    (poly_var 7).
Proof.
  (* needs x : U -> V and x : U, both from bottom *)
  refine (type_assignment_app (s := poly_var 3) (t := poly_var 7) _ _).
  - eapply type_assignment_inst with (s := poly_var 0). simpl. econstructor; reflexivity.
  - eapply type_assignment_inst with (s := poly_var 0). simpl. econstructor; reflexivity.
Qed.

(* ...so any two types T1,T2 that are instances of bottom (i.e. all) can be
   demanded of the two occurrences independently. *)

(* ---------- Fact C: mutual instance direction sanity ---------- *)
(* A type is not an instance of a strictly larger type, and type substitution
   never decreases size. This is the size argument used to argue mutual
   instance => equal up to renaming. *)
Fixpoint psize (t : poly_type) : nat :=
  match t with
  | poly_var _ => 1
  | poly_arr s t => 1 + psize s + psize t
  | poly_abs s => 1 + psize s
  end.

Lemma psize_subst_ge : forall sigma t, psize t <= psize (subst_poly_type sigma t).
Proof.
  intros sigma t; induction t; simpl; auto; try lia.
Admitted.

## Summary

**Verdict: no recursive term family tested matches LU2SemiU on the battery. The obstruction is fundamental to variable-based encodings, not a search artifact.**

### Tools/artifacts reused and repaired
- `/tmp/infer.py` (fast System F inference; sound for “typable”), `/tmp/sysf_search.py` (exact bounded search), `/tmp/semi.py` (LU2 brute force) all exist and run.
- **`/tmp/gt_small.pkl` is unreliable.** It labels `((1 1),0,0)` unsolvable, but that triple *is* solvable (`φ(0)=arr(φ(1),φ(1))`, both inequalities hold identically). I rebuilt and re-verified a 14-triple battery directly with the brute forcer; it matches the trusted facts, e.g. `(arr00,atom0,atom0)` U, `(arr00,atom1,atom1)` S, `(arr01,atom0,atom1)` U, `(arr01,atom2,atom3)` S, `(atom0,arr00,arr00)` S, `(arr11,atom0,atom0)` S.
- **Found and fixed a de Bruijn bug in the prior `explore_enc.py` style harness**: atoms encoded as `Var(d+n)` were captured by template/constructor binders (depth of the *template* lambda was not counted), so many “results” were meaningless. Corrected harness: `/tmp/mywork/fixed.py` (symbolic atom markers resolved with true binder depth).

### Searches run
1. Free atoms, 22 recursive constructors × 20 combination templates: every candidate types unsolvable `b02=((0 0),0,0)` and `b03=((0 1),0,1)`.
2. Bound atoms (atoms bound by outer lambdas, both original and capture-free resolution), same constructor/template grid: no perfect candidate; best decided 4/5 discriminating triples and the *sole* failure was always `b02` (wrongly typable).
3. “Rigidified” atoms: outer atom binders applied to closed `I`/`K` combinators, so the atom variable’s scheme is forced to a type of the argument. Still `b02` typable.
4. Direction 5 `(λx.xx) N`, `(λx.xxx) N`, `(λx.x(xx)) N`, `K`-self variants with `N` from all constructors/templates: no match; `b02` typable, or unknown at bounds.
5. `(λz. z (E t)) (E s)` forcing gadget as constructor and as top template (directions 2–3): no match.

**Best family found** (`/tmp/mywork/fixed.py`): atoms as outer λ-bound variables; `E(arr u v)=λx.λy. x (E u) (E v)`; top template `λz. ((z E(s)) E(t0)) E(t1)`. For the unsolvable `b02=((0 0),0,0)` the exact term is
```
(\x.(\x.(((\x.(\x.((x1 x3) x3))) x1) x1)))
```
and for the solvable `b10=((1 1),0,0)`:
```
(\x.(\x.(\x.(((\x.(\x.((x1 x3) x3))) x2) x2))))
```
Both are typable (infer, node_limit 100k, B=6, J=2), so the family fails exactly on the atom-sharing pair.

### Strongest obstruction (theory + experiments agree)
- Any variable (free, or λ-bound) can be given environment/domain type `bottom = ∀a.a`, making every instance requirement `T ⪯ scheme` vacuous. Hence variables used as atoms are unconditional wildcards; a shared variable cannot enforce the occurs-check that drives unsolvability.
- Rigidifying a bound atom via `(λv. BODY) R` does not fix this: the argument `R` can always be generalized, so the domain can be chosen poly-abs-headed (e.g. `∀a.a→a` for `R = λy.y`), which again allows independent instantiation at each occurrence. No term context forces a variable’s scheme to be non-polymorphic, because lambda domains and environment entries are existentially chosen.
- The only genuine rigid facts are that a lambda’s type strips to an arrow, and occurs-failures arise when a *term* is applied to itself (Omega). These constrain types of whole terms, not shared atom variables; they cannot distinguish `(arr00,atom0,atom0)` from `(arr11,atom0,atom0)`, which differ only in variable identity.

### Recommendation
A correct reduction cannot be a structurally uniform “encode term u into term E(u)” family with atoms as variables. It must use a self-referential forcing gadget where the applied argument is itself a compound encoding whose typability at the forced domain recursively encodes the constraint (e.g. `(λz. z (E t)) (E s)` with `E s`, `E t` lambdas whose domains are constrained by further gadgets), so that the shared atom identity becomes a shared *type equation* rather than a variable occurrence. Files: `/tmp/mywork/fixed.py`, `/tmp/mywork/search2.py`, `/tmp/mywork/rigid.py`, `/tmp/mywork/search4.py`. `/workspace/Task.v` untouched.

## Status

I did not close the proof, and I did not edit `/workspace/Task.v` (nor any support file). Below is what I could verify rigorously, the strongest partial construction, and the precise obstruction that stops it. The short version: the two “ground truths” in the prompt are true (and are easier than advertised — they are consequences of one central substitution), but the proposed big-scheme/`gen`-over-fresh-atoms architecture does **not** encode LU2SemiU; it encodes a strictly weaker, decidable-looking “independent substitutions” problem. I isolate the missing ingredient with two concrete triples that any correct `M` must separate.

## 1. Ground truths 1 and 2: verified, with the real reason

Let `W = σ` be the valuation `σ a = arr a a`. Then `W` is literally a substitution (`W(atom a)=arr a a`, `W(arr u v)=arr (W u)(W v)`), and:

* `σ` is **central**: for every valuation `τ`, `τ(σ u) = σ(τ u)`. (Atom case: `τ(arr a a)=arr(τ a)(τ a)=σ(τ a)`; then induction.)
* `σ` is **injective** on terms: `σ u = σ v ⇒ u=v` (`σ(atom a)` is an `arr` whose children are atoms, `σ(arr u v)` is an `arr` whose children are `arr`s, so constructors match; then IH).

These two facts give both ground truths immediately:

* If `(φ,ψ₀,ψ₁)` solves `(s,t₀,t₁)`, then applying `σ` to `ψᵢ(φ s)=φ tᵢ` and using centrality gives `ψᵢ(φ(σ s))=φ(σ tᵢ)`, so the same `(φ,ψᵢ)` solves the `W`-image. Conversely centrality plus injectivity recovers the original equation from the `W`-image equation. So ground truth 1 holds exactly.
* Ground truth 2 also holds, but with **`X = φ` itself**: `σ∘φ` is a solution with the same `ψᵢ`, and `(σ∘φ)(a)=arr(φ a)(φ a)`. So “solutions are `X∘W`” is not a new normal-form theorem; it is centrality plus associativity, and the inner `X` is just the original `φ`. In particular it does **not** give an atomic or otherwise simpler inner substitution, matching the prompt’s warning.

This matters: the square form gives no leverage on the hard part; it is a relabelling of the same solution.

## 2. A real, usable gadget: the monomorphic equality term

In `SysF.v` de Bruijn style (all `U,V` assumed closed; otherwise a `ren_term`/shift for `pure_term` must be added, since `SysF.v` defines none):

```coq
Definition I  : pure_term := pure_abs (pure_var 0).                  (* fun z => z *)
Definition K2 : pure_term := pure_abs (pure_abs (pure_var 1)).       (* fun a b => a *)
Definition EQ (U V : pure_term) : pure_term :=
  pure_app
    (pure_abs (pure_app (pure_app K2 (pure_app (pure_var 0) U))
                        (pure_app (pure_var 0) V)))
    I.
```

Typing behaviour (provable by inversion on `type_assignment`): if `Γ ⊢ EQ U V : Z`, then `Γ ⊢ U : Z` and `Γ ⊢ V : Z`; conversely if `U,V` both have type `Z` under `Γ`, then `Γ ⊢ EQ U V : Z`. The point is that `I` forces the bound `h` to have type `Z→Z`, hence both `h U` and `h V` force `U,V : Z`. This is the only sound “force two subterms to have the same type” primitive I found.

## 3. The candidate architecture and the strongest partial construction

The most one can get from `⊥ = ∀a.a` without the hard step is:

1. Bind arbitrary type carriers with `λ` and `⊥`:
   `M = (fun x_{a1} => … => (fun w => (fun x_s => (fun x_0 => (fun x_1 => BODY) g) g) g) g) g …`
   Each `(fun x => BODY) g` is typable for *any* type `P` of `x`, because `g:⊥` can be instantiated at `P`; this is the only legitimate “choose `φ(a)`” mechanism.
2. Force component structure with a recursive checker `FC(C,u)` (over the ambient `x_a`):
   * `FC(C, atom a) = EQ C x_a`
   * `FC(C, arr u v) = (fun z => K2 (FC z u) (FC (C z) v)) g`
     Under binders `C` must be shifted; `z` is the fresh binder. `FC z u` forces `z`’s type to be the `u`-encoding and `FC (C z) v` forces `C z`’s type to be the `v`-encoding, so `C` is forced to have type `arr (enc u)(enc v)`.
   Then `BODY = K2 (FC x_s s) (K2 (FC x_0 t₀) (FC x_1 t₁))` forces the three carriers to be the encodings of `s,t₀,t₁` over the shared atom carriers `x_a`. This part is sound.

At this point the shared images `φ(a)=type(x_a)` are forced, and both `φ(s)` and `φ(tᵢ)` are available as types of terms. The remaining step is to force `ψᵢ(φ s)=φ tᵢ`. The natural attempt is to use a `g`-occurrence: `inst ⊥` at `φ(s)`, `gen` the fresh variables (legal at a `g`-occurrence because its own environment entry is `⊥`, and the `g` subderivation does not touch the rest of `Γ`), then `inst` by `ψᵢ`, then `EQ` with `x_i`. This does produce, for any finite substitution `σᵢ`, a term of type `σᵢ(φ s)`, and `EQ` forces `σᵢ(φ s)=φ(tᵢ)`.

**But this is not LU2SemiU.** `σᵢ` is an independent substitution on the free variables of `φ(s)`; the definition requires `σᵢ = ψᵢ∘φ`. The term constrains only the final type `σᵢ(φ s)`, not that `σᵢ` factors through `φ`. Two concrete triples show the gap is real, one in each direction:

* `P1 = (atom 0, arr(atom 0)(atom 0), arr(atom 0)(atom 0))`.
  LU2SemiU solvable: `φ=id`, `ψ(0)=arr 0 0`. But `s` and `t₀` are **not unifiable** (`0 = arr 0 0` is an occurs check). So a one-layer big scheme `∀a. B(s(a),t(a))` (one instantiation shared by all components) is too strong and rejects `P1`.
* `P2 = (arr(atom 0)(atom 0), atom 0, atom 0)`.
  LU2SemiU unsolvable: if `φ(0)=T`, then `φ(s)=arr T T` and the equation is `ψᵢ(arr T T)=T`; writing `T=arr U U` gives `U=arr(ψᵢ U)(ψᵢ U)` with `|U|<|T|`, an infinite descent in size. But the **relaxed** system with independent substitutions is solvable: take `φ(0)=arr 0 0`, `ψ₀=ψ₁=id`, giving `arr 0 0 = arr 0 0`. So a two-layer scheme with independent instantiations for the `s`- and `t`-variables is too weak and accepts `P2`.

Thus a correct `M` must sit strictly between the one-layer and two-layer encodings; neither `∀a.B(s(a),t(a))` nor `∀a.∀b.B(s(b),t(a))` works.

## 4. Where exactly the proof breaks

The missing step is a pure-term gadget `G(x_s, x_i)` with the following property:

> Any typing of `G` yields a *single type* `A` (the type of `x_s`) together with a substitution `Θ` such that `type(x_i) = Θ(A)` and `Θ = ψ∘φ`, where `φ` is the shared image assignment on the atoms of `s`.

No such `G` follows from `type_assignment`:

* `inst` applies **one** substitution to the whole body of the scheme; it can give `ψ(φ(s))` or `φ(t)` but not independent substitutions with a *common base*.
* `gen` at a `λ`-bound or free variable cannot substitute free variables of its declared type. Recomputing the rule `type_assignment_gen` shows why: the premise environment is `map (ren_poly_type S) Γ`, so generalizing a declared type `P` produces `poly_abs (ren S P)`; the new binder is vacuous with respect to `P`’s free variables. Only at a `⊥`-typed `g`-occurrence, where the type being generalized comes from an `inst` rather than from the environment, does `gen` generalize real free variables. I isolate the missing ingredient with two concrete triples that any correct `M` must separate.

## 1. Ground truths 1 and 2: verified, with the real reason

Let `W = σ` be the valuation `σ a = arr a a`. Then `W` is literally a substitution (`W(atom a)=arr a a`, `W(arr u v)=arr (W u)(W v)`), and:

* `σ` is **central**: for every valuation `τ`, `τ(σ u) = σ(τ u)`. (Atom case: `τ(arr a a)=arr(τ a)(τ a)=σ(τ a)`; then induction.)
* `σ` is **injective** on terms: `σ u = σ v ⇒ u=v` (`σ(atom a)` is an `arr` whose children are atoms, `σ(arr u v)` is an `arr` whose children are `arr`s, so constructors match; then IH).

These two facts give both ground truths immediately:

* If `(φ,ψ₀,ψ₁)` solves `(s,t₀,t₁)`, then applying `σ` to `ψᵢ(φ s)=φ tᵢ` and using centrality gives `ψᵢ(φ(σ s))=φ(σ tᵢ)`, so the same `(φ,ψᵢ)` solves the `W`-image. Conversely centrality plus injectivity recovers the original equation from the `W`-image equation. So ground truth 1 holds exactly.
* Ground truth 2 also holds, but with **`X = φ` itself**: `σ∘φ` is a solution with the same `ψᵢ`, and `(σ∘φ)(a)=arr(φ a)(φ a)`. So “solutions are `X∘W`” is not a new normal-form theorem; it is centrality plus associativity, and the inner `X` is just the original `φ`. In particular it does **not** give an atomic or otherwise simpler inner substitution, matching the prompt’s warning.

This matters: the square form gives no leverage on the hard part; it is a relabelling of the same solution.

In `SysF.v` de Bruijn style (all `U,V` assumed closed; otherwise a `ren_term`/shift for `pure_term` must be added, since `SysF.v` defines none):

```coq
Definition I  : pure_term := pure_abs (pure_var 0).                  (* fun z => z *)
Definition K2 : pure_term := pure_abs (pure_abs (pure_var 1)).       (* fun a b => a *)
Definition EQ (U V : pure_term) : pure_term :=
  pure_app
    (pure_abs (pure_app (pure_app K2 (pure_app (pure_var 0) U))
                        (pure_app (pure_var 0) V)))
    I.
```

Typing behaviour (provable by inversion on `type_assignment`): if `Γ ⊢ EQ U V : Z`, then `Γ ⊢ U : Z` and `Γ ⊢ V : Z`; conversely if `U,V` both have type `Z` under `Γ`, then `Γ ⊢ EQ U V : Z`. The point is that `I` forces the bound `h` to have type `Z→Z`, hence both `h U` and `h V` force `U,V : Z`. This is the only sound “force two subterms to have the same type” primitive I found.

## 3. The candidate architecture and the strongest partial construction

   `M = (fun x_{a1} => … => (fun w => (fun x_s => (fun x_0 => (fun x_1 => BODY) g) g) g) g) g …`

2. Force component structure with a recursive checker `FC(C,u)` (over the ambient `x_a`):

1	From Stdlib Require Import List.
2	
3	(* pure lambda-terms M, N, .. *)
4	Inductive pure_term : Type :=
5	  | pure_var : nat -> pure_term
6	  | pure_app : pure_term -> pure_term -> pure_term
7	  | pure_abs : pure_term -> pure_term.
8	
9	(* polymorphic types s, t, ..*)
10	Inductive poly_type : Type :=
11	  | poly_var : nat -> poly_type
12	  | poly_arr : poly_type -> poly_type -> poly_type
13	  | poly_abs : poly_type -> poly_type.
14	
15	(* system F type environments *)
16	Definition environment := list poly_type.
17	
18	(* function composition *)
19	Definition funcomp {X Y Z} (g : Y -> Z) (f : X -> Y) :=
20	  fun x => g (f x).
21	
22	(* stream cons *)
23	Definition scons {X: Type} (x : X) (xi : nat -> X) :=
24	  fun n => match n with | 0 => x | S n => xi n end.
25	
26	(* polymorphic type variable renaming *)
27	Fixpoint ren_poly_type (xi : nat -> nat) (s : poly_type) : poly_type  :=
28	  match s return poly_type with
29	  | poly_var x => poly_var (xi x)
30	  | poly_arr s t => poly_arr (ren_poly_type xi s) (ren_poly_type xi t)
31	  | poly_abs s => poly_abs (ren_poly_type (scons 0 (funcomp S xi)) s)
32	  end.
33	
34	(* polymorphic type variable substitution *)
35	Fixpoint subst_poly_type (sigma : nat -> poly_type) (s : poly_type) : poly_type  :=
36	  match s return poly_type with
37	  | poly_var s => sigma s
38	  | poly_arr s t => poly_arr (subst_poly_type sigma s) (subst_poly_type sigma t)
39	  | poly_abs s => poly_abs (subst_poly_type (scons (poly_var 0) (funcomp (ren_poly_type S) sigma)) s)
40	  end.
41	
42	(*
43	  Curry-style System F Type Assignment predicate
44	  Γ ⊢ M : τ is (type_assignment Γ M τ)
45	*)
46	Inductive type_assignment : environment -> pure_term -> poly_type -> Prop :=
47	| type_assignment_var {Gamma x t} :
48	    nth_error Gamma x = Some t ->
49	    type_assignment Gamma (pure_var x) t
50	| type_assignment_app {Gamma M N s t} :
51	    type_assignment Gamma M (poly_arr s t) -> type_assignment Gamma N s ->
52	    type_assignment Gamma (pure_app M N) t
53	| type_assignment_abs {Gamma M s t} :
54	    type_assignment (s :: Gamma) M t ->
55	    type_assignment Gamma (pure_abs M) (poly_arr s t)
56	| type_assignment_inst {Gamma M s t} :
57	    type_assignment Gamma M (poly_abs s) ->
58	    type_assignment Gamma M (subst_poly_type (scons t poly_var) s)
59	| type_assignment_gen {Gamma M s} :
60	    type_assignment (map (ren_poly_type S) Gamma) M s ->
61	    type_assignment Gamma M (poly_abs s).
62	
63	Definition SysF_TYP : pure_term -> Prop :=
64	  fun M => exists Gamma t, type_assignment Gamma M t.

3	Inductive term : Set :=
4	  | atom : nat -> term
5	  | arr : term -> term -> term.
6	
7	Definition valuation : Set := nat -> term.
8	
9	(* substitute atoms n of a term t by (f n) *)
10	Fixpoint substitute (f: valuation) (t: term) : term :=
11	  match t with
12	  | atom n => f n
13	  | arr s t => arr (substitute f s) (substitute f t)
14	  end.
15	
16	(* The two inequalities share the same left-hand side s. *)
17	Definition LU2SemiU : term * term * term -> Prop :=
18	  fun '(s, t0, t1) => exists (φ ψ0 ψ1: valuation),
19	    substitute ψ0 (substitute φ s) = substitute φ t0 /\ substitute ψ1 (substitute φ s) = substitute φ t1.

1	Definition reduction {X Y} (f : X -> Y) (P : X -> Prop) (Q : Y -> Prop) :=
2	  forall x, P x <-> Q (f x).

5	Definition reduces {X Y} (P : X -> Prop) (Q : Y -> Prop) :=
6	  exists f : X -> Y, reduction f P Q.
7	Notation "P ⪯ Q" := (reduces P Q) (at level 70).

## Report

**Verdict: no term family matching all seven discriminators was confirmed within the time budget.** The bounded exact tools were rebuilt and validated, but the System F oracle could not be pushed to the type-size bound the search requires without exploding, so the full ~20-template × size-40 grammar sweep did not complete. ### Tools recreated (all in /tmp/suwork)
- `/tmp/suwork/semi.py` — brute-force `LU2SemiU`: enumerates φ over images from the term universe of size ≤3 over atoms 0..5 for every atom in `s∪t0∪t1`, then one-way matching `ψ_i(φ s)=φ t_i`.
- `/tmp/suwork/sysf.py`, `/tmp/suwork/sysf2.py` — bounded Curry-System-F typability. `sysf2.py` is the better one: bottom-up possible-types sets, closure under inst (`∀s → s[a:=T]`) and gen (`t ↦ ∀.ren_S t`), var/app/abs rules, lambda domains enumerated from a bounded universe. Direction of soundness is reliable (it only accepts genuine rule applications).
- `/tmp/suwork/fasttest.py` — validation harness with per-term timeouts.

### Verified semi-unification battery
`semi.py` exactly reproduced all supplied labels:
- `(atom0, arr00, arr00)` SOLVABLE — φ(0)=atom0, identity matchings.
- `(arr00, atom0, atom0)` UNSOLVABLE — no φ in the size-≤3 image space works (occurs check `ψ(arr Y Y)=Y`).
- `(arr01, atom0, atom1)` UNSOLVABLE; `(arr01, atom2, atom3)` SOLVABLE (φ(2)=φ(3)=arr φ(0) φ(1)).
- `(arr00, atom1, atom1)`, `(arr11, atom0, atom0)`, `(atom0, arr00, arr00)` all SOLVABLE.

### System F oracle validation
With modest bounds (type nodes ≤5, 2 type vars, domains ≤3), `sysf2.py` correctly classifies: `I`, `K`, `(λx.xx)`, `(λx.x)(λy.y)`, `λx.λy.x`, `λx.xxx` typable; `Ω=(λx.xx)(λx.xx)` untypable. Note these confirm the given fact: `λx.xx` *is* System-F typable (x : ∀a.a), so occurs-check intuition from simple types does not transfer directly.

### Where it breaks
The oracle is **sound but incomplete at low bounds**. Example: `λx.λy. x y` is typable only with domain `∀a.a` (bottom), producing the nested type `(∀a.a)→(τ→σ)` of size ≥6; at the fast bound (nodes ≤5) it is reported untypable (false negative). Raising the bound to nodes =8 (1776 types / 570 quantifier types with 2 type vars) makes the inst/gen closure and domain enumeration blow past 120 s (I killed the run). Exact-bounded search at the necessary size was therefore not achievable in the remaining minutes; I did not get a trustworthy full-grammar verdict.

### Best partial family and precise failure
The only family the supplied gadgets directly support is the single-shared-scheme FC/EQ family:

```
M(s,t0,t1) = (fun x => Λ) ARG
FC(x, atom a)      = EQ x x_a
FC(x, arr u v)     = (fun z => K2 (FC z u) (FC (x z) v)) BOT
EQ U V             = (fun h => K2 (h U) (h V)) I,   I=(fun z=>z), K2=(fun a b=>a)
Λ                  = conjunction of EQ (FC x s) (FC x t_i)
```

This forces `type(x) = enc(φ s)` and then equates it with `enc(φ t_i)`, i.e. it enforces `φ s = φ t_i`, with **no** ψ_i. To get `ψ_i` one must use `x` at an instantiated type on the s-side only. But both the s-occurrence and the t-occurrence are subterms of the same `x` with the same scheme, so every inst/gen/self-application (`x x`, `x x x`) applies to both sides symmetrically: any σ you can realize satisfies `σ(φ s)=φ t_i` only by also transforming the t-side, giving `σ∘φ` on both sides rather than `ψ_i∘φ` on the left and `φ` on the right. Introducing a second variable `y` for the t-side restores the asymmetry but also decouples y's type from x's, so the shared φ is lost. This is exactly the stated KEY GAP (cannot realize ψ∘φ asymmetrically). Under the W/squares normalization (φ(a)=arr(X)(X)), the P1-vs-P2 distinction is precisely the occurs check `ψ(arr Y Y)=Y`, and the same shared-scheme mechanism that blocks P2 also cannot discharge the `(arr01,atom2,atom3)` side without also binding the t-side.

Bottom line: the obstruction is real and was reproduced; a family in the searched grammar could not be certified, and the precise missing ingredient is an asymmetric, s-side-only realization of the semi-substitution ψ across two occurrences that still share φ.

  (forall n, f n = g n) -> substitute f t = substitute g t.

Definition shift_term (t : term) : term := substitute (fun n => atom (S n)) t.
Definition shift_val (f : valuation) : valuation := fun n => shift_term (f n).
Definition up_val (g : valuation) : valuation :=
  fun n => match n with 0 => atom 0 | S k => shift_term (g k) end.

Lemma shift_term_substitute : forall (f : valuation) (t : term),
  shift_term (substitute f t) = substitute (shift_val f) t.

  apply substitute_ext; intro n; reflexivity.

From Stdlib Require Import List.

(* pure lambda-terms M, N, .. *)
Inductive pure_term : Type :=
  | pure_var : nat -> pure_term
  | pure_app : pure_term -> pure_term -> pure_term
  | pure_abs : pure_term -> pure_term.

(* polymorphic types s, t, ..*)
Inductive poly_type : Type :=
  | poly_var : nat -> poly_type
  | poly_arr : poly_type -> poly_type -> poly_type
  | poly_abs : poly_type -> poly_type.

(* system F type environments *)
Definition environment := list poly_type.

(* function composition *)
Definition funcomp {X Y Z} (g : Y -> Z) (f : X -> Y) :=
  fun x => g (f x).

(* stream cons *)
Definition scons {X: Type} (x : X) (xi : nat -> X) :=
  fun n => match n with | 0 => x | S n => xi n end.

(* polymorphic type variable renaming *)
Fixpoint ren_poly_type (xi : nat -> nat) (s : poly_type) : poly_type  :=
  match s return poly_type with
  | poly_var x => poly_var (xi x)
  | poly_arr s t => poly_arr (ren_poly_type xi s) (ren_poly_type xi t)
  | poly_abs s => poly_abs (ren_poly_type (scons 0 (funcomp S xi)) s)
  end.

(* polymorphic type variable substitution *)
Fixpoint subst_poly_type (sigma : nat -> poly_type) (s : poly_type) : poly_type  :=
  match s return poly_type with
  | poly_var s => sigma s
  | poly_arr s t => poly_arr (subst_poly_type sigma s) (subst_poly_type sigma t)
  | poly_abs s => poly_abs (subst_poly_type (scons (poly_var 0) (funcomp (ren_poly_type S) sigma)) s)
  end.

(*
  Curry-style System F Type Assignment predicate
  Γ ⊢ M : τ is (type_assignment Γ M τ)
*)
Inductive type_assignment : environment -> pure_term -> poly_type -> Prop :=
| type_assignment_var {Gamma x t} :
    nth_error Gamma x = Some t ->
    type_assignment Gamma (pure_var x) t
| type_assignment_app {Gamma M N s t} :
    type_assignment Gamma M (poly_arr s t) -> type_assignment Gamma N s ->
    type_assignment Gamma (pure_app M N) t
| type_assignment_abs {Gamma M s t} :
    type_assignment (s :: Gamma) M t ->
    type_assignment Gamma (pure_abs M) (poly_arr s t)
| type_assignment_inst {Gamma M s t} :
    type_assignment Gamma M (poly_abs s) ->
    type_assignment Gamma M (subst_poly_type (scons t poly_var) s)
| type_assignment_gen {Gamma M s} :
    type_assignment (map (ren_poly_type S) Gamma) M s ->
    type_assignment Gamma M (poly_abs s).

Definition SysF_TYP : pure_term -> Prop :=
  fun M => exists Gamma t, type_assignment Gamma M t.

(* Author: Andrej Dudenhefner. From SemiUnification/SemiU.v. *)

Inductive term : Set :=
  | atom : nat -> term
  | arr : term -> term -> term.

Definition valuation : Set := nat -> term.

(* substitute atoms n of a term t by (f n) *)
Fixpoint substitute (f: valuation) (t: term) : term :=
  match t with
  | atom n => f n
  | arr s t => arr (substitute f s) (substitute f t)
  end.

  fun '(s, t0, t1) => exists (φ ψ0 ψ1: valuation),
    substitute ψ0 (substitute φ s) = substitute φ t0 /\ substitute ψ1 (substitute φ s) = substitute φ t1.

From Stdlib Require Import List.
Require Import SysF SemiU Reduction.

(* --- Auxiliary semi-unification substitution lemmas --- *)

Definition square_atom (n : nat) : term := arr (atom n) (atom n).

Fixpoint square_term (t : term) : term :=
  match t with
  | atom n => square_atom n
  | arr u v => arr (square_term u) (square_term v)
  end.

Lemma substitute_substitute : forall (f g : valuation) (t : term),
  substitute g (substitute f t) = substitute (fun n => substitute g (f n)) t.
Proof.
  intros f g t; induction t; simpl; [reflexivity|].
  now rewrite IHt1, IHt2.
Qed.

Lemma substitute_square_term : forall (f : valuation) (t : term),
  substitute f (square_term t) = substitute (fun n => arr (f n) (f n)) t.
Proof.
  intros f t; induction t; simpl; [reflexivity|].
  now rewrite IHt1, IHt2.
Qed.

Lemma substitute_ext : forall (f g : valuation) (t : term),
  (forall n, f n = g n) -> substitute f t = substitute g t.
Proof.
  intros f g t H; induction t; simpl; [apply H|now rewrite IHt1, IHt2].
Qed.

Lemma square_term_arr : forall (u : term), exists a b, square_term u = arr a b.
Proof.
  intros u; destruct u; simpl.
  - exists (atom n), (atom n); reflexivity.
  - exists (square_term u1), (square_term u2); reflexivity.
Qed.

Lemma square_term_inj : forall (t u : term), square_term t = square_term u -> t = u.
Proof.
  induction t as [n | t1 IH1 t2 IH2]; intros [m | u v] H; simpl in H.
  - injection H as H1 _. subst. reflexivity.
  - destruct (square_term_arr u) as [x [y Hxy]].
    injection H as H1 _. rewrite <- H1 in Hxy. discriminate.
  - destruct (square_term_arr t1) as [x [y Hxy]].
    injection H as H1 _. rewrite H1 in Hxy. discriminate.
  - injection H as H1 H2. subst.
    rewrite (IH1 u H1), (IH2 v H2). reflexivity.
Qed.


Lemma square_term_substitute : forall (f : valuation) (t : term),
  square_term (substitute f t) = substitute (fun n => square_term (f n)) t.
Proof.
  intros f t; induction t; simpl.
  - reflexivity.
  - rewrite IHt1, IHt2; reflexivity.
Qed.

Lemma square_term_as_subst : forall (t : term),
  square_term t = substitute (fun n => arr (atom n) (atom n)) t.
Proof.
  intros t; induction t; simpl; [reflexivity|now rewrite IHt1, IHt2].
Qed.


(* --- Shifting a solution (renaming all image atoms up by one) --- *)

Definition shift_term (t : term) : term := substitute (fun n => atom (S n)) t.
Definition shift_val (f : valuation) : valuation := fun n => shift_term (f n).
Definition up_val (g : valuation) : valuation :=
  fun n => match n with 0 => atom 0 | S k => shift_term (g k) end.

Lemma shift_term_substitute : forall (f : valuation) (t : term),
  shift_term (substitute f t) = substitute (shift_val f) t.
Proof.
  intros f t. unfold shift_term, shift_val. rewrite substitute_substitute. reflexivity.
Qed.

Lemma substitute_up_shift : forall (g : valuation) (t : term),
  substitute (up_val g) (shift_term t) = shift_term (substitute g t).
Proof.
  intros g t. unfold shift_term.
  rewrite substitute_substitute.
  rewrite substitute_substitute.
  apply substitute_ext; intro n.
  unfold up_val. simpl. unfold shift_term. reflexivity.
Qed.

Lemma shift_solution : forall (phi psi0 psi1 : valuation) (s t0 t1 : term),
  substitute psi0 (substitute phi s) = substitute phi t0 ->
  substitute psi1 (substitute phi s) = substitute phi t1 ->
  substitute (up_val psi0) (substitute (shift_val phi) s) = substitute (shift_val phi) t0 /\
  substitute (up_val psi1) (substitute (shift_val phi) s) = substitute (shift_val phi) t1.
Proof.
  intros phi psi0 psi1 s t0 t1 H0 H1. split.
  - rewrite <- (shift_term_substitute phi s).
    rewrite substitute_up_shift. rewrite H0.
    rewrite shift_term_substitute. reflexivity.
  - rewrite <- (shift_term_substitute phi s).
    rewrite substitute_up_shift. rewrite H1.
    rewrite shift_term_substitute. reflexivity.
Qed.


(* --- Basic System F typing of combinators --- *)

Lemma type_assignment_I : forall (Gamma : environment) (s : poly_type),
  type_assignment Gamma (pure_abs (pure_var 0)) (poly_arr s s).
Proof.
  intros Gamma s.
  apply type_assignment_abs.
  apply type_assignment_var. simpl. reflexivity.
Qed.

Lemma type_assignment_K : forall (Gamma : environment) (a b : poly_type),
  type_assignment Gamma (pure_abs (pure_abs (pure_var 1))) (poly_arr a (poly_arr b a)).
Proof.
  intros Gamma a b.
  apply type_assignment_abs.
  apply type_assignment_abs.
  apply type_assignment_var. simpl. reflexivity.
Qed.


(* --- Type-level renaming lemmas --- *)

Lemma ren_poly_type_ext : forall (T : poly_type) (xi xj : nat -> nat),
  (forall n, xi n = xj n) -> ren_poly_type xi T = ren_poly_type xj T.
Proof.
  induction T as [n | a IHa b IHb | c IHc]; intros xi xj H; simpl.
  - now rewrite H.
  - now rewrite (IHa xi xj H), (IHb xi xj H).
  - f_equal.
    assert (Hup : forall n, scons 0 (funcomp S xi) n = scons 0 (funcomp S xj) n).
    { intro k; destruct k; simpl; [reflexivity|]; unfold funcomp; simpl; now rewrite H. }
    rewrite (IHc _ _ Hup). reflexivity.
Qed.

Lemma ren_poly_type_comp : forall (T : poly_type) (xi xj : nat -> nat),
  ren_poly_type xi (ren_poly_type xj T) =
  ren_poly_type (fun n => xi (xj n)) T.
Proof.
  induction T as [n | a IHa b IHb | c IHc]; intros xi xj; simpl.
  - reflexivity.
  - now rewrite (IHa xi xj), (IHb xi xj).
  - f_equal.
    rewrite (IHc (scons 0 (funcomp S xi)) (scons 0 (funcomp S xj))).
    apply ren_poly_type_ext. intro n. destruct n; simpl; [reflexivity|].
    unfold funcomp; simpl; reflexivity.
Qed.

(* --- Target --- *)

Theorem reduction : LU2SemiU ⪯ SysF_TYP.

- System F (Curry style): `Inductive pure_term := pure_var : nat -> pure_term | pure_app : pure_term -> pure_term -> pure_term | pure_abs : pure_term -> pure_term.` `Inductive poly_type := poly_var : nat -> poly_type | poly_arr : poly_type -> poly_type -> poly_type | poly_abs : poly_type -> poly_type.` environment = list poly_type. ren_poly_type and subst_poly_type as in SysF.v (de Bruijn; note subst_poly_type sigma (poly_abs s) = poly_abs (subst_poly_type (scons (poly_var 0) (funcomp (ren_poly_type S) sigma)) s)).

  var: nth_error Gamma x = Some t -> Gamma |- pure_var x : t
  app: Gamma |- M : poly_arr s t -> Gamma |- N : s -> Gamma |- pure_app M N : t
  abs: (s::Gamma) |- M : t -> Gamma |- pure_abs M : poly_arr s t
  inst: Gamma |- M : poly_abs s -> Gamma |- M : subst_poly_type (scons t poly_var) s
  gen: (map (ren_poly_type S) Gamma) |- M : s -> Gamma |- M : poly_abs s
- `SysF_TYP M := exists Gamma t, type_assignment Gamma M t.`
- Target: construct an explicit computable `reduce : term*term*term -> pure_term` and prove for all p, LU2SemiU p <-> SysF_TYP (reduce p). No axioms, no Admitted, no classical axioms.

2. A useful reformulation: LU2SemiU(s,t0,t1) iff exists phi, both substitute phi t0 and substitute phi t1 are instances (under some psi_i) of substitute phi s, i.e. exists phi psi0 psi1, psi_i(substitute phi s) = substitute phi ti.
3. Free/bound term variables in Curry System F are extremely flexible: any application-only term is typable (assign variables polymorphic type poly_abs (poly_var shifted appropriately), e.g. for a λ-bound x one can take x : poly_abs (poly_var 0) = ∀a.a and each occurrence instantiates independently). Ω = (λx.xx)(λx.xx) is NOT typable, but λx.xx itself IS typable (at poly_arr (poly_abs (poly_var 0)) B for any B). The central difficulty of the Wells reduction is ruling out "polymorphic escapes" (a variable of type ∀a.a) and realizing the common substitution phi asymmetrically.

(c) Validate candidates on small instances where LU2SemiU status can be brute-forced (write a small Python script in /tmp with -I, enumerating finite valuations over bounded terms) and where System F typability can be searched with a bounded proof search or a known sound inference procedure.

4	Inductive pure_term : Type :=
5	  | pure_var : nat -> pure_term
6	  | pure_app : pure_term -> pure_term -> pure_term
7	  | pure_abs : pure_term -> pure_term.

9	(* polymorphic types s, t, ..*)
10	Inductive poly_type : Type :=
11	  | poly_var : nat -> poly_type
12	  | poly_arr : poly_type -> poly_type -> poly_type
13	  | poly_abs : poly_type -> poly_type.
14	
15	(* system F type environments *)
16	Definition environment := list poly_type.
17	
18	(* function composition *)
19	Definition funcomp {X Y Z} (g : Y -> Z) (f : X -> Y) :=
20	  fun x => g (f x).
21	
22	(* stream cons *)
23	Definition scons {X: Type} (x : X) (xi : nat -> X) :=
24	  fun n => match n with | 0 => x | S n => xi n end.

26	(* polymorphic type variable renaming *)
27	Fixpoint ren_poly_type (xi : nat -> nat) (s : poly_type) : poly_type  :=
28	  match s return poly_type with
29	  | poly_var x => poly_var (xi x)
30	  | poly_arr s t => poly_arr (ren_poly_type xi s) (ren_poly_type xi t)
31	  | poly_abs s => poly_abs (ren_poly_type (scons 0 (funcomp S xi)) s)
32	  end.

35	Fixpoint subst_poly_type (sigma : nat -> poly_type) (s : poly_type) : poly_type  :=
36	  match s return poly_type with
37	  | poly_var s => sigma s
38	  | poly_arr s t => poly_arr (subst_poly_type sigma s) (subst_poly_type sigma t)
39	  | poly_abs s => poly_abs (subst_poly_type (scons (poly_var 0) (funcomp (ren_poly_type S) sigma)) s)
40	  end.

43	  Curry-style System F Type Assignment predicate
44	  Γ ⊢ M : τ is (type_assignment Γ M τ)
45	*)
46	Inductive type_assignment : environment -> pure_term -> poly_type -> Prop :=
47	| type_assignment_var {Gamma x t} :
48	    nth_error Gamma x = Some t ->
49	    type_assignment Gamma (pure_var x) t
50	| type_assignment_app {Gamma M N s t} :
51	    type_assignment Gamma M (poly_arr s t) -> type_assignment Gamma N s ->
52	    type_assignment Gamma (pure_app M N) t
53	| type_assignment_abs {Gamma M s t} :
54	    type_assignment (s :: Gamma) M t ->
55	    type_assignment Gamma (pure_abs M) (poly_arr s t)
56	| type_assignment_inst {Gamma M s t} :
57	    type_assignment Gamma M (poly_abs s) ->
58	    type_assignment Gamma M (subst_poly_type (scons t poly_var) s)
59	| type_assignment_gen {Gamma M s} :
60	    type_assignment (map (ren_poly_type S) Gamma) M s ->
61	    type_assignment Gamma M (poly_abs s).

(* --- Auxiliary semi-unification substitution lemmas --- *)

Definition square_atom (n : nat) : term := arr (atom n) (atom n).
